Glue — grammar

bù vs méi

Template: bù + Verb (habit/intention/future); méi + Verb (completed past) / méiyǒu (for "not have")

bù = "don't, won't"; méi = "didn't, haven't"

Wǒ jīntiān méi chī zǎofàn.
Wǒ bù hē jiǔ.

Foreigner traps

  • Refusing with méi: 'I'm not going' is bù qù — méi qù means you didn't go (past).
  • Yesterday with bù: completed past negatives take méi — Wǒ zuótiān méi qù, never bù qù.
  • méiyǒu does double duty: before a verb it negates the past, but alone it means 'not have' — Wǒ méiyǒu qián is 'I have no money'.

bù vs méi — the deepest writeup found — 2,500 words on the split, with pinyin'd examples.

shì…de focus

Template: Subject + shì + (how/when/where/why) + Verb + de

highlights the detail of a known past event

Wǒ shì zuò fēijī lái de.
Tā shì qùnián jiéhūn de.

Foreigner traps

  • Opening with shì…de about an event the listener doesn't know yet — it presupposes shared knowledge and sounds like an interrogation; establish the event first.
  • Word order: shì rides the detail, de closes the verb — wǒ zuò fēijī shì lái de is wrong.
  • It frames PAST events; using it for plans ('next week I'm coming by train') is ungrammatical — plain future + zài lái.

Native notes — bù vs méi, and haggling without being that person

The méi…le combo = plans changed

Méi qù le means 'not going AFTER ALL' — the le flags a change from the expected. Tā jīntiān méi lái le drifts toward complaint. This is why bù/méi confusion matters socially: bù lái is a decision, méi lái le reads like betrayal of a plan.

bù vs méi — the deepest writeup found — 2,500 words on the split, with pinyin'd examples.

shì…de is an answer, not an opener

Natives deploy shì…de when the event is already common knowledge and a detail is being nailed down. Cold-opening with Nǐ shì zěnme lái de? is fine (the arrival is visible), but asking about something unknown with shì…de sounds like an interrogation. Get the event on the table first, then shì…de the details.

shì…de construction — full guide — Cleft framing plus drill-downs on time/place/manner/agent.

Two sorries, two jobs

duìbuqǐ is for actual fault (stepping on a foot, being late). bù hǎo yìsi is embarrassment — the social-lubricant word you'll use ten times more: declining an invitation, accepting a compliment, asking a favor. It softens everything, and using duìbuqǐ for all of it sounds stiffly formal.

Apologizing in degrees — The graded apology ladder, duìbuqǐ through bàoqiàn.

Cultural: haggling is a duet, not a fight

The market script — Zhège zěnme mài? → price → Zài xiāngyīn yìdiǎn ma! → counter — is playful theater, and the ma is what keeps it smiling. Xiāngyīn is the local word for cheap (standard layer: piányi yìdiǎn). The rule stands: scanner = fixed (supermarkets, chain stores, anywhere there's a price gun); no scanner = the dance is open. Trying to haggle at a convenience store marks you instantly.
